texts: On day 460 of Year 2, the keepers of the Middle Row lit the lanterns of the Middle Row at sundown.
The mire-essence in the lanterns held salt-bloom.
A cold wind struck the Middle Row at night.
The mist-light attracted a handful of nightmoths.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lanterns.
Keepers collected the silken threads from the lanterns at dawn on day 461 of Year 2.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the first cauldron on day 461 of Year 2.
Mire-essence formed in the first cauldron by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in a clay vessel.
The keepers of the Middle Row drew the stored mire-essence at sundown on day 461 of Year 2.

q1_issues.issue: "The mire-essence in the lanterns held salt-bloom" is a containment stative transitive, which the instruction set assigns Agent (its own example "the tank holds forty litres"), reserving Holder for own/have/lack only.

The of-phrase restrictor in "the keepers of the Middle Row" is dropped entirely — sk_keeper_1 gets no Possession/PartOf link to middle_row, although the parallel "the lanterns of the Middle Row" does get one.

"The lanterns stayed lit" emits only the per-member reified-state rule; the mandated flat half of the continuation-copular dual-emit (as the per-member rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_lantern_1) (Member $x lit))) is missing, so no member's "is it lit?" can bind.
"left silken threads" takes Patient although depositing leaves the threads unchanged — the change test (and its default-to-Theme fallback) selects Theme.
(Ordinal sk_cauldron_1 1 cauldron) puts the entity's own class in the scale slot, which the instruction set licenses only for an associated event or an explicit "-est" dimension.

"boiled ... in sea-water" is slotted as Instrument although the PP answers "where/in what medium" and its preposition is "in", where the instruction set's oblique rules point to Location or the preposition-named (In ...).

q2_gaps: ordinal day-of-year dating ("on day 460 of Year 2") — (Day <n>) is defined only as the day-of-month granularity of a calendar expression, leaving a day numbered within the year with no distinct licensed form
an ordinal that ranks a plain object noun with no associated event and no "-est" dimension ("the first cauldron") — the instruction set supplies no licensed filler for Ordinal's scale slot

a distributive per-member rule whose predicate is TRANSITIVE with a plural/group object ("the keepers lit the lanterns", "the nightmoths left silken threads") — every distributive example given is intransitive, and the instruction set never says whether the object distributes too, so the shared-symbol convention yields "each keeper lit the whole lantern group"

cross-part-of-speech lemma collision — "lit" (verb) and "mist-light" (noun head) both lemmatize to the symbol light, and the instruction set offers no sense-disambiguation, so the lighting event class and the noun genus share one symbol
review.notes: Aside from the role and dual-emit slips above the passage is well tracked — witness identity (two distinct keeper groups, two distinct mire-essence witnesses), the compound decompositions (silken_thread with its material-adjective modifier genus, clay_vessel and nightmoth without noun-modifier genera), "by evening" as TimeAtMost, and the creation/positioning events correctly taking Location on the event only. One further omission: the participial modifier in "the stored mire-essence" gets no atom, though coreference to sk_mire_essence_2 arguably discharges it.

issues.reason: Thematic roles bounds Holder to possession verbs "own / have / lack" and gives "the tank holds forty litres" as the stative transitive that still takes Agent, so (Holder sk_hold_1 sk_mire_essence_1) asserts a possession relation the rule bars for exactly this verb.

Core patterns forbids silently dropping a stated restriction ("omitting it widens the claim"), and the licensed carrier plainly exists — the parse itself emits (Possession sk_lantern_1 middle_row) for the parallel "the lanterns of the Middle Row" — so the keepers' of-phrase is an omitted licensed atom, not gap territory.

The continuation copular ("stayed lit") mandates the reified state plus the flat atom (Dual-emit; Resultatives), which on a plural group becomes the per-member rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_lantern_1) (Member $x lit)); only the reified half was emitted, so no member's "is it lit?" can bind.

Depositing leaves the threads themselves unaltered, so the "does the object itself change?" test — and its explicit default-to-Theme fallback — yields Theme; Patient asserts a change the leaving does not make.

This mistakes a coverage gap for a defect (the reviewer files it as gap 2 as well): Ordinal's scale slot has no licensed filler for a plain object noun with no associated event or "-est" dimension, and (Ordinal sk_cauldron_1 1 cauldron) asserts nothing false — it records the stated rank, which Core patterns forbids silently dropping.

Instrument's own gloss covers "a tool, substance or conduit" as the means, and the preposition-named oblique is reserved for PPs naming what the activity is about or directed at, so sea-water as the medium the boiling is done in is a licensed reading (Location is already taken by the cauldron in the same clause).

gaps_confirmed: Day-of-year ordinal dating ("on day 460 of Year 2"): (Day n) is defined as the day granularity of a calendar expression paired with (Month ...), so a day numbered within the year has no distinct licensed form.

An ordinal ranking a plain object noun with no associated event and no "-est" dimension ("the first cauldron"): no licensed filler exists for Ordinal's scale slot — this is the hole behind refuted issue 4.

A per-member distribution rule whose predicate is TRANSITIVE with a plural/group object ("the keepers lit the lanterns", "the nightmoths left silken threads"): every distributive example in the instruction set is intransitive and nothing says whether the object co-distributes, so the shared-symbol convention makes each member act on the whole group.

Cross-part-of-speech lemma collision: the verb "lit" lemmatizes to light and the noun head of "mist-light" also gives light, and lemmatization offers no sense split, so the lighting event class and the noun genus share one symbol.
new_gaps: A medium PP naming the substance an action is performed in ("boiled the threads in sea-water") has no decision rule: Instrument is defined by means, Location by place, and the preposition-named oblique by aboutness, so nothing selects among them for a medium — which is why issue 5 is underdetermined.

A bare mass direct object later taken up by a definite anaphor ("burned mire-essence" ... "The mire-essence in the lanterns ..."): Existential reserves the bare class symbol for a non-specific object, but a bare class symbol gives the later definite nothing to attach its predications to, so the two rules pull opposite ways and no licensed form covers both.
adjudication.defect_summary: Issue 0: the compliant form is (Agent sk_hold_1 sk_mire_essence_1) — a stative transitive keeps Agent, Holder being own/have/lack only. Issue 1: add (Possession sk_keeper_1 middle_row) beside (GroupOf sk_keeper_1 keeper), exactly as the parallel lantern phrase is handled. Issue 2: add the flat half of the dual-emit as the per-member rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_lantern_1) (Member $x lit)) (STV 1.0 0.9) beside the reified state. Issue 3: the compliant role is (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_thread_1).
adjudication.notes: The passage is otherwise well tracked — two distinct keeper groups, two distinct mire-essence witnesses, clean compound decompositions, "by evening" as TimeAtMost, and Location-on-the-event-only for the creating/positioning clauses. Beyond the filed gap, the six transitive distribution rules arguably over-assert rather than merely improvise (each keeper lighting the whole lantern group, each lantern producing the one mist-light), which a re-parse should settle rather than replicate.
